definitions.explanation: The age at which employees are required to retire from a company, typically 60-65 in Japan. Upon reaching this age, employees leave their regular positions.

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{来年|らいねん}{定年|ていねん}を{迎|むか}える。
examples.english: My father reaches retirement age next year.

examples.japanese: {定年|ていねん}が65{歳|さい}に{引|ひ}き{上|あ}げられた。
examples.english: The retirement age was raised to 65.

examples.japanese: {定年|ていねん}{後|ご}も{働|はたら}き{続|つづ}ける{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: More people are continuing to work after retirement age.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
{定|てい} (fixed, set) + {年|ねん} (age, year)

Literally "set age" - the predetermined age for retirement.

RETIREMENT AGE IN JAPAN:
- Traditional: 60{歳|さい}
- Current trend: 65{歳|さい} (due to aging society)
- Some companies: 70{歳|さい} or later

RELATED WORDS:
- {定年退職|ていねんたいしょく} - mandatory retirement
- {早期退職|そうきたいしょく} - early retirement
- {再雇用|さいこよう} - rehiring (after retirement age)
- {嘱託|しょくたく} - contract employee (post-retirement)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {定年|ていねん}を{迎|むか}える - to reach retirement age
- {定年|ていねん}まで{働|はたら}く - to work until retirement
- {定年|ていねん}{延長|えんちょう} - extending retirement age
- {定年|ていねん}{引上|ひきあ}げ - raising retirement age

CULTURAL NOTE:
With Japan's aging population and labor shortage, many companies are:
- Raising {定年|ていねん} to 65 or 70
- Offering {再雇用|さいこよう} programs
- Eliminating mandatory retirement altogether
